proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(A\) has full column rank and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), every feasible vector has a unique representation \(b=b^0+Nz\).  For fixed \(x\), suppress \(x\) and write
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=(b^0)'\Gamma b^0+2z'g+z'Hz,
\qquad g=N'\Gamma b^0.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(v\in\ker H\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv)=\|\Gamma^{1/2}Nv\|^2.
\]
Thus \(\Gamma Nv=0\) and \(v'g=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0\).  Since \(H\) is a finite-dimensional symmetric matrix, \((\ker H)^\perp=\operatorname{range}H\), so \(g\in\operatorname{range}H\).  The normal equation \(Hz=-g\) is solvable, and its unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}H\) is \(z^\star=-H^\dagger g\).  Substitution in (3) proves
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0,
\qquad A'b^\star=\omega,
\qquad N'\Gamma b^\star=g-HH^\dagger g=0.
\tag{4}
\]
Under fixed rank and the separated positive spectrum, \(H^\dagger\) is obtained by applying the Borel function \(z\mapsto z^{-1}\mathbf 1\{z\ge\kappa\}\) to the measurable symmetric matrix \(H\); hence (4) is measurable.  Two minimizers differ by \(Nv\) with \(v\in\ker H\).  The preceding argument shows that this is exactly an element of \(\ker\Gamma\cap\ker A'\), proving the uniqueness assertion.

If \(\Gamma\) is positive definite, the Lagrange equations are \(\Gamma b=A\lambda\) and \(A'b=\omega\).  Full column rank of \(A\) makes \(A'\Gamma^{-1}A\) positive definite.  Solving the two equations gives
\[
b=\Gamma^{-1}A(A'\Gamma^{-1}A)^{-1}\omega,
\]
as claimed.

There are finitely many support points, folds, score coordinates, and retained cells.  The lower support-mass bound and retained-cell overlap imply that every relevant training-cell count is of order \(n\) in probability.  Each coordinate of the corrected score is a finite sum of outcome residuals multiplied by propensity ratios bounded in terms of \(\varepsilon\), plus its denominator correction.  Fixed \(T\), the conditional fourth-moment envelope, and Jensen's inequality therefore give
\[
\sup_x E_P[\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x]<\infty.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently each coordinate of \(\Psi_P\Psi_P'\) has finite conditional variance.  Chebyshev's inequality for each cell average and a union bound over the fixed collection show that the oracle conditional first and second moments, and hence the oracle conditional covariance, have error \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) simultaneously over support points and folds.

On the clipped overlap region, the maps entering Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) are finite sums and products, and every reciprocal propensity has derivative bounded by a constant depending only on \(\varepsilon\).  Add and subtract the oracle propensity and regression in every coordinate.  The mean-value inequality followed by H\"older's inequality gives
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
\le O_P(n^{-1/2})+C\{r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}\}.
\tag{6}
\]
All vector and matrix norms are equivalent here because both the support and the score dimension are fixed.  This proves the first assertion and also proves the claim about estimating the finitely many required conditional expectations by cell averages.

With parametric cell first stages, (6) gives \(r_{\Gamma,n}=O(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), then
\[
\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\to0,
\qquad r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a}).
\]
The loading-perturbation lemma then gives rank recovery.  Finally,
\[
r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2
=O(n^{-1+2a}+n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2})
\]
for \(0<a<1/4\).  For continuously distributed \(X\), a conditional covariance learner regresses products of scores.  The displayed fourth-moment premise gives only a conditional second moment for those products and supplies neither a smoothness class nor the higher-tail control needed for an \(L_4(P_X)\) nonparametric rate.  Thus no continuous-covariate rate follows from the stated premises, exactly as the proposition records.

Put \(E_\ell(x)=\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)-\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Since \(N'N=I\), the variational characterization of ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
\max_j|\lambda_j\{N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\}-\lambda_j\{H(x)\}|
\le E_\ell(x).
\tag{7}
\]
For all large \(n\), \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\).  A false positive from the zero cluster then requires \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), and a false negative from the positive cluster requires \(E_\ell(x)\ge\kappa-\tau_n>\tau_n\).  Markov's inequality and the \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance rate therefore give, uniformly over the fixed number of folds,
\[
P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}
\le \tau_n^{-4}\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}.
\tag{8}
\]

By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), \(g=N'\Gamma b^0\) belongs to \(\operatorname{range}H\).  Set \(z^0=H^\dagger g\), so \(Hz^0=g\), and set \(\widehat g=N'\widehat\Gamma b^0\).  The spectral gap and the conditional envelope bound \(\|z^0\|\) uniformly.  Let \(\widehat P_\tau=\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat H\).  The exact identity
\[
\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat g
=\widehat P_\tau z^0
+\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\{(H-\widehat H)z^0+(\widehat g-g)\}
\tag{9}
\]
shows the claimed stability.  Indeed, the retained inverse has norm at most \(\tau_n^{-1}\), while \(\|\widehat H-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat g-g\|\le C E_\ell\).  If \(E_\ell\le\tau_n\), then (7), the gap \(\kappa\), and the eigenvector equations imply
\(\|\widehat P_\tau-P_H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 2E_\ell/(\kappa-E_\ell)\), where \(P_H\) projects onto \(\operatorname{range}H\).  This inequality follows by projecting \(\widehat H\widehat v=\widehat\lambda\widehat v\) onto \(\ker H\) and, symmetrically, projecting \(Hv=\lambda v\) onto the retained null space.  If \(E_\ell>\tau_n\), the trivial projector bound \(2\le2E_\ell/\tau_n\) applies.  Since \(P_Hz^0=z^0\), (9) yields for every \(x\)
\[
\|\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)-b^\star(x)\|
\le C\,E_\ell(x)/\tau_n.
\tag{10}
\]
Taking \(L_4(P_X)\), and then \(L_2(P_X)\), norms proves the stated \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)\) bounds.  Threshold separation makes them \(o_P(1)\).  On the correctly selected range, the retained eigenvalues are at least \(\kappa/2\); using this bound in (9) and the preceding projector calculation removes \(\tau_n^{-1}\) and gives the sharper \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\) local rate.

Write \(\eta=(p,m)\), \(\alpha_P(X)=K_P(X)^\dagger r_P(X)\), and
\[
\mu_P(O)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O).
\]
Conditional on a training complement, the validation observations are independent of all foldwise estimates by the cross-fitting assumption.  In each inverse-propensity residual term, add and subtract the true regression.  To display the resulting calculation, let \(M_{a,s,k}=\sum_{u=g}^t m_{a,s,u}\), let \(\widehat M_{a,s,k}\) be its estimated counterpart, and let \(B_{k,c}\) denote the bracketed numerator in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Conditional expectation and the definition of \(q_{k,c}\) give the exact identity
\[
\begin{split}
E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}-B_{k,c}\mid X]
={}&\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{g,0}}{\widehat p_{g,0}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{g,0,k}-M_{g,0,k})\\
&+\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,1}}{\widehat p_{c,1}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,1,k}-M_{c,1,k})\\
&+\left(p_{g,1}-\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,0}}{\widehat p_{c,0}}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,0,k}-M_{c,0,k}).
\end{split}
\]
Every parenthesized coefficient on the right is Lipschitz in \(\widehat p-p\) on the overlap set.  Because the number of cells and periods is fixed, H\"older's inequality gives
\[
|P\{\mu(O;\widehat\eta)-\mu(O;\eta)\}|
\le C\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,4}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{15}
\]
Here the last equality uses the stipulated cell-average first stages.  The empirical target-share denominator is treated separately below.

For the correction signal, Lemma \(\ref{lem:orthogonal-normal-signal}\) and the observable restrictions give
\[
\|E_P[\widehat S^{-\ell}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{per}}(O;\eta)=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O).
\tag{16}
\]
Proposition \(\ref{prop:complete-normal-finite-support-rates}\) gives
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\alpha^{-\ell}-\alpha_P\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2+a})=o_P(1).
\tag{17}
\]
The moment bound (11), nuisance consistency, and (17) imply
\[
\|\widehat\alpha^{-\ell}(X)'\widehat S^{-\ell}
-\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (16)--(17) make the conditional mean of the left term in (18) \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  Conditional Chebyshev inequality applied fold by fold to (15) and (18), followed by summation over the fixed number of folds, therefore gives
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\{\mu_P-\alpha_P(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\}
+o_P(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{19}
\]
apart from the target-share denominator contribution.

For \(k=(g,t)\), overlap implies \(\pi_{g,1}\ge\varepsilon\), and the empirical share obeys
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})+O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{20}
\]
The mean numerator of every reference coordinate in target block \(k\) is \(\pi_{g,1}\theta_k(P)\).  Multiplying (20) by that numerator and by \(\omega_k\) shows that the denominator contribution to (19) is
\[
-\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}
(\mathbb P_n-P)\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{21}
\]
By Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), combining (19) and (21) changes \(\mu_P-E_P\mu_P\) exactly into \(\psi_P^0\).  Definition \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) then yields
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\{\psi_P^0(O_i)-\alpha_P(X_i)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O_i)\}+o_P(1)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{22}
\]
The summands in (22) are mean zero, have variance \(V_{\mathrm{can}}>0\), and have finite second moment by (11).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) gives the asserted Gaussian limit.

The estimated influence value in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) contains both the denominator correction in (21) and the orthogonal complete-normal correction.  Root-\(n\) consistency of the preliminary ratios and shares, (18), and the conditional weak law give
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\longrightarrow_P E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}^2]=V_{\mathrm{can}}.
\]
Division by its positive probability limit preserves the standard-normal limit in (22), and the definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) gives limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  Finally, Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) identifies \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) as the canonical gradient, so the attained variance is the full pointwise semiparametric bound.

Fix either declared constant comparator and write \(b=b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\).  Both \(b\) and \(b^\star(X)\) satisfy \(A'b=\omega\).  Every coordinate of \(\Psi\) in target block \(k\) has conditional mean \(h_k(X)\), so both aggregate scores have conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\).  Put \(d=b-b^\star=Nz\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\), and hence, pointwise,
\[
b'\Gamma b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma b^\star
=2d'\Gamma b^\star+d'\Gamma d=d'\Gamma d=z'Hz.
\tag{23}
\]
The conditional variance formula and integration prove the first displayed identity in the proposition.  Adding the identity \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}\) from Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) proves the full-loss formula.

Moreover,
\[
N'\Gamma b=N'\Gamma(b-b^\star)=Hz.
\tag{24}
\]
If (24) is zero, then (23) is zero.  Conversely, if the expected quantity in (23) is zero, nonnegativity gives \(z'H(X)z=0\) almost surely.  Positive semidefiniteness then gives \(H(X)z=0\), so (24) vanishes.  This proves the aggregate equality characterization, including singular cases.

It remains to characterize full equality.  The difference \(b'\Psi-\psi_P^0\) is a measurable clean-comparison contrast and hence belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\) by Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\).  Therefore \(b'\Psi\) is another ambient gradient of the same target, and its projection onto \(\mathcal T_P\) is the unique canonical gradient.  The complete-normal tangent theorem says that
\[
\mathcal T_P^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}:a\text{ measurable}\}}.
\]
Thus \(b'\Psi\in\mathcal T_P\) if and only if it is orthogonal to every such multiple.  Conditional expectation shows that this is equivalent to
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b'\Psi\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{25}
\]
An ambient gradient has variance equal to the canonical bound if and only if its orthogonal normal component is zero, so (25) is also equivalent to full efficiency.  By Definition \(\ref{def:projection-diagnostic}\), (24) and (25) are exactly the two reported population residuals.

The construction gives \(p_{a,s}(x)=1/6\) for every retained \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), and hence \(\pi_{2,1}=1/6\).  Outcomes are bounded because \(|Z_t^{\mathrm w}|\le1/8\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\).  Consistency holds by construction.  The treatment term vanishes when \(s=0\), proving no ineligible effect, and before adoption, proving no anticipation.  The distribution of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) depends on \((G,X)\) but not on \(S\), so the eligibility gap of every untreated increment is zero within every cohort.  This proves every conditional parallel-gap restriction and therefore \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

The conditional means satisfy \(m_{2,s,2}=s\delta\) and \(m_{3,s,3}=s\delta\), with every other retained one-step treatment term zero.  Since both residual signs have conditional mean zero, all three conditional DDD contrasts and both targets equal \(\delta\).  The target-cell term \(q-\theta\) in the corrected score is therefore zero.  Put \(a=3/4\).  Direct substitution in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}.
\end{array}
\tag{26}
\]
Every row has conditional probability \(1/6\), and
\[
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]
=E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
\qquad
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\]
Multiplying the entries in (26) row by row proves
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{27}
\]

Feasibility is \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\) and \(b_3=\omega_2\), so write
\[
b(q)=(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2)'.
\]
Equation (27) gives
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}
=\frac{3}{16}(4q-2xr\omega_2),
\qquad
\frac{d^2}{dq^2}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac34>0.
\]
Thus \(q^\star(x)=xr\omega_2/2\), proving the formula for \(b^\star\).  Also
\[
\det\!\left(
\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}-\lambda I\right)
=(2-\lambda)\{(2-\lambda)^2-(1+r^2)\}.
\]
The stated eigenvalues follow.  Since \(r^2<7/9\), the smallest is strictly larger than \((3/16)(2-4/3)=1/8\).

Because \(E[X]=0\), the unconditional \((2,3)\) covariance in (27) is zero.  Both the joint constant problem and the first OVS block are uniquely minimized at \(q=0\); the third coordinate is fixed.  Hence both named constant loadings are \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)'\).  Their displacement from \(b^\star(X)\) is \((-Xr\omega_2/2,Xr\omega_2/2,0)'\), and direct evaluation gives the aggregate loss
\[
E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
=\frac{3}{16}\,2\left(\frac{r\omega_2}{2}\right)^2
=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{28}
\]
For an arbitrary deterministic feasible \(b(q)\), the conditional quadratic is a quadratic in \(q\) with second derivative \(3/4\) and minimizer \(Xr\omega_2/2\).  Therefore its excess over the conditional minimum is \(3\{q-Xr\omega_2/2\}^2/8\).  Since \(E[X]=0\) and \(X^2=1\), integration gives
\[
E_P[(b(q)-b^\star)'\Gamma(b(q)-b^\star)]
=\frac{3q^2}{8}+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32},
\tag{29}
\]
which is strictly positive for every constant \(q\) because \(r\omega_2\ne0\).

Finally, the only nonzero observable restriction row in this architecture is the period-two equality between cohorts \(3\) and \(\infty\).  Thus \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) has one coordinate, \(Z_{2;3,\infty}\).  The kernel of \(A'\) is spanned by \((1,-1,0)'\), and (26), or direct subtraction of the raw scores, gives
\[
R_{(2,2),3}-R_{(2,2),\infty}=-Z_{2;3,\infty}.
\tag{30}
\]
Equation (30) and the nonzero scalar convention for \(N\) prove \(\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp\) by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\).  Hence \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=0\), and Proposition \(\ref{prop:equality-frontier}\) turns (28)--(29) into full-bound losses.  Substitution of \(r=\omega_2=1/2\) gives \(3/512\).

If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), and after the fixed target ordering the incidence matrix \(A\) is the identity.  Therefore \(\ker(A')=\{0\}\), \(N\) has no columns under the declared convention, and \(A'b=\omega\) has one solution.  The conditional and constant loading problems consequently coincide.

If \(X\) is degenerate, \(\Gamma(X)=\Gamma\) almost surely.  More explicitly, the conditional-mean identity \(E_P[\Psi\mid X]=Ah(X)\) and total covariance give
\[
\Omega=E_P[\Gamma(X)]+\operatorname{Var}_P\{Ah(X)\}=\Gamma,
\]
where the last variance vanishes because \(X\) is degenerate.  Thus the conditional and constant quadratic programs have the same objective.  Write every feasible loading as \(b=b^0+Nz\).  Since \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\) and \(Nz\in\ker A'\), these terms are Euclidean-orthogonal.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) selects the solution \(z=-H^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0\) in \(\operatorname{range}H\), which is the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of the normal equations.  This is exactly the Moore--Penrose convention defining \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).

The final sentence is a scope statement rather than an identification claim: Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) shows that a score loading is canonical only after projection against the full period-specific normal space.  Hence no external just-identified influence function is equated to the present one without a theorem-level source and matching tangent restrictions.

There are finitely many support points, cells, periods, normal coordinates, target coordinates, and folds.  The lower support-mass and overlap conditions make every training count used by a conditional cell average of order \(n\) in probability.  Every coordinate of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) is a finite sum of outcome residuals multiplied by inverse propensities bounded by \(\varepsilon^{-1}\); the same is true of \(\psi_P^0\), apart from bounded conditional means and the target-share correction.  Fixed \(T\), the conditional fourth-moment envelope, and Jensen's inequality imply, at this fixed law,
\[
\sup_{x:P_X(x)>0}E_P[\|Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\|^4+|\psi_P^0|^4\mid X=x]<\infty.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus every coordinate of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}Z_P^{\mathrm{per}\prime}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\psi_P^0\) has finite conditional variance.  Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound give root-\(n\) accuracy for all oracle training-cell averages.

The cell-average estimates of \(p\), \(m\), \(\pi\), and the preliminary ratios are jointly \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Identity (1) in Lemma \(\ref{lem:orthogonal-normal-signal}\) shows, in particular, that replacing \(Z\) by the orthogonal signal \(\widehat S\) creates no first-order regression-centering drift: its conditional mean error is \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  The finite-dimensional mean-value inequality and H\"older's inequality applied to the second moments and cross-moments then give
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat K^{-\ell}-K_P\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
+\max_\ell\|\widehat r^{-\ell}-r_P\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{12}
\]

At a support point \(x\), let \(\kappa_P(x)\) be the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(K_P(x)\), with value \(+\infty\) at rank zero.  Finiteness of the support implies
\[
\underline\kappa_P=\min_{x:P_X(x)>0}\kappa_P(x)>0.
\tag{13}
\]
This is a pointwise consequence, not a uniform model restriction.  The eigenvalue variational inequality used in (7) and (12) show that, once \(\tau_n<\underline\kappa_P/2\), a rank error requires \(\|\widehat K^{-\ell}(x)-K_P(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\tau_n\).  Fourth-power Markov inequality and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\) therefore prove rank recovery uniformly over the finite support and folds.

On the recovery event, all retained eigenvalues exceed \(\underline\kappa_P/2\).  Repeating identity (9) with \((K_P,r_P)\) in place of \((H,g)\) yields
\[
\|\{\widehat K^{-\ell}_\tau\}^{\dagger}\widehat r^{-\ell}-K_P^\dagger r_P\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{14}
\]
Using only \(\|\{\widehat K^{-\ell}_\tau\}^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\tau_n^{-1}\) gives the unconditional conservative bound \(O_P(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n)\).  With \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), this is \(O_P(n^{-1/2+a})\), and
\[
n^{-1+2a}=o(n^{-1/2})\quad(0<a<1/4),
\qquad
n^{-1/2+a}n^{-1/2}=o(n^{-1/2})\quad(0<a<1/2).
\]
The declared range \(0<a<1/4\) proves all remaining assertions.

added_lemmas.statement: For every period-specific row \(e\), every candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) with retained propensities clipped below by \(\varepsilon/2\), and the signal in Definition \(\ref{def:orthogonal-complete-normal-signal}\), the conditional drift is exactly a sum of propensity--regression products. Consequently its Gateaux derivative with respect to either nuisance at the truth is zero. Under the observable period-specific equalities, \(g_e(X)=0\) and \(S_e(O;\eta)=Z^{\mathrm{per}}_{e,P}(O)\) almost surely. Moreover, \[\|E_P[S^{\mathrm{per}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\mid X]-g(X)\|_{P_X,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widetilde p-p\|_{P_X,4}\|\widetilde m-m\|_{P_X,4}.\]
added_lemmas.justification: The complete-normal correction must remain orthogonal after regression centering is estimated.
added_lemmas.gap: A raw plug-in residual contrast has first-order regression-centering drift; adding the estimated restriction level cancels it algebraically.
added_lemmas.consumer: The finite-support canonical estimator and its complete-normal moment-rate proposition use this product-bias identity.

added_lemmas.statement: Consider the obsolete projection rule that subtracts only the closed span of measurable multiples of \(N'R_P\) from each centered dictionary coordinate.  There is a bounded finite-support interior law with \(T=4\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{4,\infty\}\), and degenerate \(X\), together with a bounded centered coordinate \(v\), for which that rule returns a nonzero element of \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\), rather than an element of \(\mathcal T_P\).  Hence projection against the aggregate clean-comparison contrast alone is not a valid tangent-score sieve in the period-specific model.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Construct the law as follows.  Let \(X\) be degenerate and let \((G,S)\) be uniform on \(\{2,4,\infty\}\times\{0,1\}\).  Conditional on every cell, draw independent Rademacher variables \(U\) and \(V\), independent also of \(S\), and take the period-two and period-three untreated outcome residuals to be \(U/8\) and \(V/8\), with all conditional means zero; add any fixed treatment effect only in the target eligible cell after adoption.  All outcomes are bounded, every retained cell has positive probability, and all finite-support atoms have positive mass.  Because the residual law does not depend on eligibility, both period-specific comparison equalities hold, so this is an interior law relative to the equality model.

Let \(Z_2=Z_{2;4,\infty}\) and \(Z_3=Z_{3;4,\infty}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives \(Z_2,Z_3\in\mathcal T_P^\perp\).  Independence and equal scaling give
\[
E_P[Z_2Z_3]=0,
\qquad E_P[Z_2^2]=E_P[Z_3^2]>0.
\tag{31}
\]
There are two pairwise coordinates, one for comparison cohort \(4\) and one for \(\infty\), and their cumulative difference is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(Z_2+Z_3\).  Hence the obsolete aggregate normal \(N'R_P\) spans \(Z_2+Z_3\).  Choose \(v=Z_2-Z_3\).  Equation (31) gives
\[
E_P[v(N'R_P)]=0,
\]
so the obsolete projection rule subtracts zero and returns \(v\).  Yet \(v\ne0\) by (31), and \(v\in\mathcal T_P^\perp\).  Since a closed subspace intersects its orthogonal complement only at zero, \(v\notin\mathcal T_P\).  This proves the asserted failure without invoking the corrected complete-normal gap definition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(0<r<\sqrt7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)'\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\).  In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\),
\[

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each training complement of \(I_\ell\), estimate the retained propensities and one-step regressions by \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\), and construct
\[
\widehat S_i^{-\ell}=S^{\mathrm{per}}(O_i;\widehat\eta^{-\ell}),
\qquad \widehat\eta^{-\ell}=(\widehat p^{-\ell},\widehat m^{-\ell}).
\]
Using training-sample cell averages, form the symmetrized conditional moments
\[
\widehat K^{-\ell}(x)=
\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{-\ell}\widehat S^{-\ell\prime}\mid X=x],
\qquad
\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)=
\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{-\ell}\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}\mid X=x],
\]
where
\[
\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}
=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k
\left\{\widehat R_{k,c_0(k)}^{-\ell}
-\widehat\theta_k^{-\ell}\frac{\mathbf 1_{g,1}}{\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-\ell}}\right\},
\]
and the preliminary ratios \(\widehat\theta_k^{-\ell}\) and shares \(\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-\ell}\) are computed on the training complement.  Threshold the eigenvalues of \(\widehat K^{-\ell}(x)\) at \(\tau_n\), form the Moore--Penrose inverse of the retained part \(\widehat K^{-\ell}_\tau(x)\), and set
\[
\widehat\alpha^{-\ell}(x)=
\{\widehat K^{-\ell}_\tau(x)\}^{\dagger}\widehat r^{-\ell}(x).
\]
For \(i\in I_\ell\), evaluate the cross-fitted raw ratio pseudo-outcomes \(\widehat R_i\) and the signal \(\widehat S_i^{-\ell}\), and return
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\left\{
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\alpha^{-\ell}(X_i)'\widehat S_i^{-\ell}
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat\theta_k=n^{-1}\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}\) and \(\widehat\pi_{g,1}=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\).  For \(i\in I_\ell\), define
\[
\widehat\phi_i=
\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k
\left\{\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\theta_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\widehat\pi_{g,1}}\right\}
-\widehat\alpha^{-\ell}(X_i)'\widehat S_i^{-\ell},
\]
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat\phi_i-\overline{\widehat\phi})^2,
\qquad
\overline{\widehat\phi}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\phi_i,
\]
and report the already declared Wald interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Subtracting a plug-in multiple of the raw residual normal leaves first-order regression-centering drift and the aggregate loading does not attain the full bound. The corrected map subtracts the thresholded complete-normal coefficient times the orthogonal one-step signal.

proposed.name: Orthogonal complete-normal restriction signal
proposed.construction:
For a retained cohort \(a\) and period \(u\), set
\[
d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x).
\]
For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\), define the conditional restriction level
\[
g_e(x)=d_{c,u}(x)-d_{c',u}(x).
\]
For a candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) whose retained propensity coordinates are positive, let
\[
Z_e(O;\widetilde\eta)=
\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{\widetilde p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c,1,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{\widetilde p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c,0,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{\widetilde p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c',1,u}(X)\}
+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{\widetilde p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{c',0,u}(X)\},
\]
and
\[
S_e(O;\widetilde\eta)=
\widetilde d_{c,u}(X)-\widetilde d_{c',u}(X)+Z_e(O;\widetilde\eta),
\qquad
\widetilde d_{a,u}=\widetilde m_{a,1,u}-\widetilde m_{a,0,u}.
\]
Stack these coordinates in \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\)-order as \(S^{\mathrm{per}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\), using the zero-dimensional convention when \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\) is empty.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support and every support mass is bounded below.  Use training-cell averages for all conditional moments in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\), and suppose the propensity and regression first stages are parametric cell averages.  Under retained-cell overlap, the conditional fourth-moment envelope, fixed-fold cross-fitting, \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), uniformly over the fixed number of folds,
\[
\|\widehat K^{-\ell}-K_P\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
+\|\widehat r^{-\ell}-r_P\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For each support point, thresholding recovers \(\operatorname{rank}K_P(x)\) with probability tending to one.  On the recovered ranges,
\[
\|\{\widehat K^{-\ell}_\tau\}^{\dagger}\widehat r^{-\ell}
-K_P^\dagger r_P\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\]
while the unconditional conservative threshold bound is \(O_P(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n)\). open_obligations.what_is_open: A pointwise asymptotic linear expansion for the corrected complete-normal one-step estimator of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\), including the derivative of the comparator Moore--Penrose map and the estimated growing-dimensional Riesz representer.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen premises provide population tangent projection and fixed-support rates for \(K_P^\dagger r_P\), but they do not provide an explicit closed derivative for every term of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) or a rate controlling the product of derivative-estimation error, growing sieve dimension, Gram inversion, and complete-normal first stages. Assuming that remainder is negligible would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: The population dictionary was projected against the complete period-specific normal vector, which repairs tangent membership, and the finite-support generalized-inverse rates were derived. The former aggregate-only sieve counterexample was isolated under a new theorem. Expanding the corrected gap map still leaves unboundedly many estimated derivative coordinates and comparator KKT derivatives without a declared joint rate envelope.
open_obligations.partial_result: The complete-normal projection lemma proves that every population dictionary coordinate obtained by projecting against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) lies in \(\mathcal T_P\), and Proposition \(\ref{prop:complete-normal-finite-support-rates}\) supplies pointwise finite-support rates for \(K_P^\dagger r_P\).  The obsolete aggregate-normal sieve is separately refuted by Theorem \(\ref{thm:frozen-aggregate-sieve-failure}\).  What remains is the derivative and estimated growing-dimensional Riesz-map expansion for \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\); no positive Wald claim is made.

prose_updates.tldr: The target is a fixed aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the target-indexed period-specific restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna. A finite residual basis \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) exhausts the observed tangent normal, and its Moore--Penrose projection gives the full canonical gradient. Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) remains the optimum inside the smaller aggregate pairwise-score family. In the fixed-finite-support regime, a repaired cross-fitted estimator subtracts \(\widehat\alpha(X)'\widehat S^{\mathrm{per}}\), where the augmented restriction signal has only propensity--regression product drift, and attains the full pointwise bound with a valid Wald interval. The OVS and joint constant loadings have separate aggregate and full equality equations. A bounded binary family yields the exact full-bound gain \(3/512\); positive inference for the estimated efficiency-gap functional remains open because its growing Riesz-map remainder has not been proved.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish identification, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise weighting, but do not exhaust the observed tangent space of the overidentified period-specific DDD model or analyze a learned full-normal correction. Existing staggered-DiD efficiency results do not supply the coupled eligibility-gap tangent normal.
project_justification.niche: Eligibility and staggered adoption impose simultaneous conditional restrictions period by period. Cumulative clean-comparison contrasts can span only part of their normal space, so the information bound and an attaining estimator require a complete residual basis and an orthogonal plug-in signal for its estimated centering.
project_justification.fill: The note proves observable tangent exhaustion, derives the singular complete-normal canonical projection, and separates it from conditional generalized least squares within the pairwise-score family. It constructs an explicit orthogonal restriction signal and proves pointwise attainment with cell-average learners for fixed finite covariate support. It also gives exact aggregate and full equality diagnostics and a bounded \(3/512\) witness. Gap-functional Wald inference is not claimed until its full derivative and growing Riesz remainder are controlled.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the proved attainment regime, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below. Fixed-fold training-cell averages estimate retained propensities, one-step regressions, the augmented period-specific signals \(S_e=g_e+Z_e\), and the conditional moments \(K_P(X)\) and \(r_P(X)\). Thresholding with \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\), estimates the complete-normal coefficient. The shared-cell covariance \(\Gamma_P(X)\) and \(b^\star(X)\) are learned separately for comparator diagnostics; no continuous-covariate attainment claim is made from fourth moments alone.

prose_updates.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise benchmark. The present result differs by exhausting all target-indexed period-specific DDD normals and by learning their correction through an augmented restriction signal. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie give related conditional efficiency results for staggered DiD, but their model does not imply the DDD full-data extension or eligibility-gap tangent calculation. Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; the range inclusion, quotient projection, and learned fixed-support remainder are proved here. Generic DML theory supplies the cross-fitting template but not the all-cohort shared-cell and complete-normal calculations. The bounded binary construction is a full-bound comparison because its sole period-specific normal is exactly the aggregate clean-comparison contrast.
prose_updates.interpretation: There are two precision frontiers. The first minimizes variance among feasible conditional loadings of cumulative pairwise scores and is attained by \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\). The second projects an ambient target gradient against every period-specific restriction normal and yields \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\). A comparator reaches the first frontier when \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0\); it reaches the full bound only when \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\). The fixed-support estimator reaches the second frontier by subtracting a learned multiple of the orthogonal signal \(S_e=g_e+Z_e\), not a raw plug-in residual.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at an interior law and permits singular or redundant complete-normal coordinates. Statistical attainment is proved only for fixed finite covariate support, where cell averages give root-\(n\) conditional-moment rates and a fixed-law positive spectral separation follows from finite support. Uniform inference across rank-changing laws and general continuous-covariate attainment are not claimed. The corrected efficiency-gap construction has valid population tangent coordinates, but its full derivative and estimated growing-dimensional Riesz-map remainder remain unproved, so no positive gap Wald theorem is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at interior laws satisfying all observable period-specific conditional DDD equalities and admitting an OVS full-data extension. The canonical gradient and bound are population results. Their cross-fitted attainment and pointwise Wald inference are proved for fixed finite-support covariates with support masses bounded below, cell-average first stages, and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\). The \(b^\star(X)\), OVS, and joint constant loadings are called fully efficient only when the complete-normal equation holds. The \(3/512\) witness satisfies that closure condition. Efficiency-gap pointwise inference and rank-uniform inference remain open.
